procedure.method: Read Decimal bytes as data; parse complete physical sources with bundled Acorn. Independently derive lexical declaration bindings, exact line roles, parser references/callers, call arguments/owners, assignments, constructor sites and export structure. Seven symbolic counterexamples parsed only, with seven discriminating controls.

findings.claim: All 1072 original ordered observation rows and 384 extra same-file/line occurrences are preserved. 536 rows and 344 distinct physical lines per variant.
findings.limit: Duplicate ordinal records observation occurrence only; original scanner offset/token/rule/traversal is unavailable.

findings.claim: The 16 own-constructor-related row proposals are supported by lexical clone/Decimal production, x.constructor = Decimal, the exclusive finite parser callers, and the initial prototype constructor assignment.
findings.details: 6 constructor-reference rows on 6 lines; 6 parser construction-route rows on 4 lines; 4 assignment rows on 4 lines. parseOther has one call from inner Decimal under its primitive-string branch; parseDecimal has four call sites (three in inner Decimal, one in parseOther). No parser escape reference or constructor-field write is present.
findings.limit: Local identity and numeric parsing route under ordinary language and intrinsic operations. It is not callback-free proof for tag-compatible objects, foreign public receivers, or arbitrary mutable methods.

findings.claim: 732 row proposals across 436 lines describe scalar/configuration/arithmetic/index/comparison/formatting expression roles. Independent line-role classification and candidate completeness match the I0 line proposals.
findings.details: 152 of these 436 lines contain CallExpression nodes. Numeric expression role does not certify the concrete member callee, clear an invocation elsewhere, or identify the scanner token. config enumerates precision/rounding/toExpNeg/toExpPos/maxE/minE/modulo and has a strict true/false/0/1 crypto branch.
findings.limit: These are not 732 accepted or suppressed scanner diagnostics. Property origin, coercion and member-method identity are not established by data-role classification.

findings.claim: 268 invocation-line rows on 212 lines and 56 constructor-transfer rows on 26 lines retain unresolved constructor identity.
findings.details: Each physical file contains new this.constructor (6), new x.constructor (1), new Ctor (113), new this (41), new Decimal (3) and new Uint32Array (2). This is a syntactic inventory; the two own parseOther Ctor sites are distinguished from other Ctor identities. Helpers preserve incoming constructor capabilities. Public method and static assignments expose these routes without receiver-identity checks.
findings.limit: An exported assignment or a conditional property-name match does not certify a particular supplied receiver/callee. Only concrete consumer bindings or guards could change that unknown.

findings.claim: UMD AMD-before-CJS-before-global/noConflict structure and ESM named/default Decimal exports match the physical AST.
findings.details: AMD factory returns local Decimal, but define is an external unbound identifier. ESM initializes Decimal = P.constructor = clone(DEFAULTS) and directly uses Symbol.for/Symbol.toStringTag; UMD guards Symbol in its CJS branch. No syntactic eval/Function/require/import call or import declaration was found in either physical variant.
findings.limit: No supplied host-selection or external AMD implementation evidence. Absence of a named evaluator AST is not universal capability closure. Uint32Array remains a syntactic host data-constructor descriptor, not a certified concrete host binding.

findings.claim: All 1718 call/new sites, 3070 local declaration/assignment nodes and 267 function/program graphs were independently reconciled, including callee spans, arguments, owners, incoming edges and public method assignments.
findings.details: 265 actual functions plus two program graphs. Conditional prototype-member name routes remain conditional; syntactic assignments carry no invented execution-dominance or runtime receiver proof.
findings.limit: Closed graph means this bounded physical AST, not external consumer closure.

findings.claim: The two authority-designated physical source files and the substantive read-set remained byte- and metadata-stable across the independent check window and finalization.
findings.limit: Both source files currently have nlink 1. Historical original48link lineage is unproved without its trusted manifest; this review supplies no historical lineage or whole-tree certificate.

counterexamples.limit: The installed abs body uses new this.constructor(this). A supplied receiver can select a different constructor before finalise; no assertion that this scenario ran or was an actual consumer.
Exported cos reaches new this(x).cos(); call supplies Capability as this. The actual callee identity stays unknown without consumer binding.
A closed local helper caller graph or parameter spelling Ctor does not prove the function passed is the clone-produced Decimal.
An AMD guard and a local factory returning Decimal constrain the callback, not the supplied define implementation or selected host.
isDecimalInstance permits tag-compatible inputs, then the constructor copy path calls v.d.slice(). Producer identity does not certify that supplied method.
Two Ctor identifiers on one line have distinct AST roles. Two same-line scanner observations still cannot be mapped to them from observation occurrence alone.
Matching an installed P.toString property name permits only a conditional route; it cannot prove this concrete receiver/callee is that method.
